newsitem.title: USA: Amoco may deploy some sale proceeds in Kazak.
newsitem.headline: Amoco may deploy some sale proceeds in Kazak.

text.p: Amoco Corp said that it will deploy some of the proceeds from its sale of U.S. reserves in Kazakhstan, if it is succesful in bids it has made there.
Amoco is to auction U.S. reserves of 460 million barrels of oil equivalent and 70,000 barrels of daily production, which analysts say could fetch $2.0-$2.5 billion.

"If we are succesful in our Kazakhstan bids, there could be an immediate need for capital there, similar to the situation when we acquired a 50 percent stake in Bolivian oil company Empresa Petrolera Chaco," said Richard Flurry, head of Amoco's worldwide exploration and production division.

The company has bid in a tender for Kazakhstan's Uzen oil field and recently bought a stake in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which plans to build a 990 mile pipeline from Kazakhstan's Tengiz oilfield to the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
"With the CPC stake we now have an outlet and we are negotiating for further reserves," Flurry said.

Commenting on the analysts forecasts of a $2.0-$2.5 billion price tag for the U.S. assets, Flurry said that the company aimed to maximise the price by an auction and that figure would be influenced by the mix of reserves, two-thirds natural gas and one third oil, and their location.
"A lot of the natural gas is in the western basins which have been at somewhat of a price disadvantage recently," Flury said.
He declined to give a figure for what the company would expect. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
